title: Refuse lossy integer scalar canonicalization
finding: SparseTensorEntry stores scalar values as binary64 floats. Integer input was accepted and unconditionally converted with float(...), so distinct integers such as 2**53 and 2**53+1 could collapse to the same retained float, canonical JSON and TensorView digest. Extremely large integers could also raise OverflowError outside the tensor contract's ValueError refusal domain.
primary_claim: Integer-valued sparse tensor claims are accepted only when their exact integer value survives binary64 canonicalization; lossy integers refuse before retention, and integer overflow is normalized into the existing finite-number ValueError boundary.
gardener_decision: Harden the existing SparseTensorEntry scalar boundary rather than add a Decimal/fixed-point wrapper, alternate serializer or second numeric contract. Forest and Fourfold remain authoritative; tensor remains a derived computational projection.
acceptance: 2**53 remains accepted and canonicalizes to its exact binary64 value
larger integers that are exactly representable, such as 2**60, remain accepted
2**53+1 refuses instead of aliasing the retained value and digest of 2**53
integer overflow such as 10**400 refuses as ValueError inside the tensor contract boundary
bool, string and arbitrary __float__ coercion remain refused
signed zero normalization from G1-TENSOR-01C remains unchanged
